text: A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, with orchestra:
and I'm stopped in my tracks, down on my knees. Do among us what you did among them. Work among us as you worked among them. And as you bring judgment, as you surely must, remember mercy.
retracing the old salvation route, Coming up from the south through Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Skies are blazing with his splendor, his praises sounding through the earth,
forked-lightning shooting from his hand— what power hidden in that fist!
He looks around. Nations tremble. The age-old mountains fall to pieces; ancient hills collapse like a spent balloon. The paths God takes are older than the oldest mountains and hills.
Old wilderness adversaries, Cushan and Midian, were terrified, hoping he wouldn't notice them.
Angry at old River? Were you raging at Sea when you rode horse and chariot through to salvation?
and let loose a volley of arrows. You split Earth with rivers.
They twisted in pain. Flood Waters poured in. Ocean roared and reared huge waves.
Your flashing arrows stopped them, your lightning-strike spears impaled them.
Furious, you crushed the godless nations.
to save your specially chosen people. You beat the stuffing out of King Wicked, Stripped him naked from head to toe,
and blew away his army. Scattered they were to the four winds— and ended up food for the sharks!
racing on the crest of the waves.
I stammered and stuttered. My bones turned to water. I staggered and stumbled. I sit back and wait for Doomsday to descend on our attackers.
and the strawberries don't ripen, Though the apples are worm-eaten and the wheat fields stunted, Though the sheep pens are sheepless and the cattle barns empty,
I'm turning cartwheels of joy to my Savior God.
I take heart and gain strength. I run like a deer. I feel like I'm king of the mountain! (For congregational use, with a full orchestra.)
